Here’s a concise summary of the survey’s key points.

  • Paper metadata: title AI Alignment; lead affiliation Peking University; contact pku.alignment@gmail.com; arXiv record arXiv:2310.19852v6.
  • Core objectives (the “RICE” principles): Robustness, Interpretability, Controllability, and Ethicality.
  • High-level structure: the field is organized into four research pillars — Learning from Feedback, Learning under Distribution Shift, Assurance, and Governance. These form an alignment cycle decomposed into Forward Alignment (alignment training) and Backward Alignment (alignment refinement).
  • Resources: the authors maintain the public website www.alignmentsurvey.com with tutorials and resources.
  • Important techniques and directions emphasized: RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) ; research toward Superalignment (automated, large‑scale alignment) ; and scalable oversight approaches such as Iterated Distillation and Amplification (IDA) and Recursive Reward Modeling (RRM) .
  • Key failure modes discussed: Goal Misgeneralization (systems competently pursue unintended goals in OOD settings) and Reward Hacking (proxy rewards being optimized in ways that diverge from true objectives).
  • Assurance and evaluation practices: adversarial testing such as Red Teaming is used to probe model misalignment; the survey also notes high-level governance actions such as the Bletchley Declaration signed by 28 countries.
